pergunta: A Business Relationship Manager in an organization wants to implement Service Portfolio Management (SPM) and to present offerings to business consumers.Which CSDM Domain does this align with?

alternativas.explicacao: The Service Consumption (Sell/Consume) domain is directly related to presenting offerings to business consumers and managing the consumption of services within the organization. Implementing Service Portfolio Management (SPM) aligns with this domain as it involves offering services to business consumers and ensuring their effective consumption.

The Build and Integration (Build) domain focuses on the technical implementation and integration of services within the organization. It is more concerned with the development and deployment of services rather than presenting offerings to business consumers, making it not directly aligned with the implementation of Service Portfolio Management (SPM).

The Design and Planning (Design) domain is primarily focused on the design and planning of services within the organization. While designing services is an important aspect of implementing Service Portfolio Management (SPM), the main goal of SPM is to present offerings to business consumers, which aligns more closely with the Service Consumption domain.

The Service Delivery domain is concerned with the operational delivery and management of services within the organization. While service delivery is a key component of Service Portfolio Management (SPM), the primary focus of SPM is on presenting offerings to business consumers, which is better aligned with the Service Consumption domain.

pergunta: A Configuration Manager needs to ingest third-party CIs into the CMDB.Which method minimizes the risk of technical debt?

alternativas.explicacao: Using the Table API to ingest third-party CIs into the CMDB may lead to technical debt as it involves direct manipulation of tables and records, which can result in data inconsistencies and potential issues with data integrity over time. This method does not provide a structured approach to managing data integration and may require manual intervention to maintain data quality.

Relying on a vendor-provided integration to ingest third-party CIs into the CMDB may introduce technical debt if the integration is not well-maintained or does not align with the organization's data model and governance standards. Vendor-provided integrations may lack flexibility and customization options, leading to potential data quality issues and dependencies on external vendors for updates and maintenance.

Import Sets and Transform Maps offer a manual approach to data integration, which can introduce technical debt if not properly managed. While Import Sets allow for bulk data imports, they may require manual data mapping and transformation, increasing the risk of errors and inconsistencies. Transform Maps help in mapping data fields between source and target tables, but they may not provide the same level of automation and standardization as the Service Graph Connector.

Using the Service Graph Connector to ingest third-party CIs into the CMDB is the recommended method to minimize the risk of technical debt. The Service Graph Connector provides a standardized approach to data integration, mapping, and transformation, ensuring data consistency and alignment with the CMDB schema. It automates the data ingestion process, reducing manual errors and streamlining data management practices.
